original: ΕΝ ΑΡΧΗ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν.
translation: In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth.
differences_from_web: LXX has ἐποίησεν 'made' where the Hebrew has בָּרָא 'created' (WEB)
LXX opening ἐν ἀρχῇ-style phrase 'in the beginning' matches the wording of Jn 1:1, but Genesis has no 'word'
_web_text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

original: Κύριος ἔκτισέν με ἀρχὴν ὁδῶν αὐτοῦ εἰς ἔργα αὐτοῦ,
translation: The Lord created me as the beginning of his ways, for his works,
differences_from_web: LXX 'created me' (ἔκτισεν) where Hebrew קָנָנִי is 'possessed/acquired me' (WEB 'possessed')
LXX 'as the beginning of his ways, for his works' versus WEB 'in the beginning of his work'
_web_text: “The LORD possessed me in the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old.

original: καὶ ὀφθήσεται ἡ δόξα Κυρίου, καὶ ὄψεται πᾶσα σὰρξ τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅτι Κύριος ἐλάλησεν.
translation: And the glory of the Lord will be seen, and all flesh will see the salvation of God, for the Lord has spoken.
literal_notes: τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ θεοῦ: 'the salvation of God'
differences_from_web: LXX adds 'and all flesh will see the salvation of God' (τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ θεοῦ) where the Hebrew has 'all flesh shall see it together'
LXX lacks 'together'; 'mouth of the LORD has spoken' becomes 'the Lord has spoken'
_web_text: The LORD’s glory shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken it.”
